1 | """The provider abstraction that makes FileDrive's UI backend-agnostic.
2 | 
3 | Every storage system (FileNet, local disk, Alfresco, Google Drive, Microsoft
4 | 365, Box, ...) implements `StorageProvider`. Routers never talk to a specific
5 | backend directly — they resolve the active provider for the current session
6 | and call these methods. All ids (`folder_id`, `file_id`, `version_id`) are
7 | opaque strings; each provider decides what's actually inside them (a FileNet
8 | GUID, a local integer, a Google Drive file id, ...) and nothing outside the
9 | provider should assume a shape.
10 | 
11 | Two authentication shapes exist, because they're genuinely different:
12 | 
13 | - `AuthMode.CREDENTIALS` — username/password checked directly against the
14 |   backend (FileNet, Alfresco, local disk). `authenticate()` validates them
15 |   and the same pair is cached server-side and passed back into every other
16 |   call as `creds` (a small opaque object the provider itself defines the
17 |   shape of — for these it's `{"username": ..., "password": ...}`).
18 | - `AuthMode.OAUTH` — Google Drive / Microsoft 365 / Box. There's no
19 |   authenticate(); instead `get_authorize_url()` sends the browser to the
20 |   provider's consent screen, and `complete_oauth()` exchanges the callback
21 |   code for tokens. Those tokens (access + refresh) become `creds` for every
22 |   subsequent call, refreshed transparently by the provider as needed.
23 | 
24 | `creds` is passed as a plain dict on every call rather than typed per
25 | provider, since routers are provider-agnostic and shouldn't need to import
26 | every provider's credential type. Each provider validates the shape it

1 | """AWS S3 and IBM Cloud Object Storage — IBM COS exposes an S3-compatible
2 | API (same request shapes, HMAC access-key/secret-key auth), so both are the
3 | same provider underneath with a different `endpoint_url`: AWS resolves its
4 | own regional endpoint from `region`, IBM COS needs an explicit endpoint URL
5 | (e.g. `https://s3.us-south.cloud-object-storage.appdomain.cloud`) since
6 | there's no single well-known IBM domain to derive it from.
7 | 
8 | UNVERIFIED — built against boto3's stable, extensively-documented S3 API,
9 | but there's no real AWS/IBM account or bucket in this environment to run it
10 | against. Run it against a real bucket before trusting it the way FileNet's
11 | and local disk's providers are trusted.
12 | 
13 | S3 has no real folders — only object keys, with "/" as a UI convention. So:
14 | - ids ARE the key: a folder's id is its key ending in "/", a file's id is
15 |   its key. No separate id<->key mapping needed, and it's stable across
16 |   everything (rename/move naturally change the id, same as they'd change a
17 |   FileNet path).
18 | - `get_children` uses `Delimiter="/"` so S3 itself does the "one level"
19 |   grouping (CommonPrefixes = subfolders, Contents = files) — no need to
20 |   fetch and filter the whole bucket.
21 | - A folder "exists" as a zero-byte marker object at its own key (`prefix/
22 |   name/`), the common convention every S3 console/tool uses.
23 | - No native trash or rename: delete moves to a `$Trash/` prefix (permanent
24 |   delete actually removes it); rename/move is copy-then-delete, recursive
25 |   for folders (copy every object under the old prefix, then batch-delete

27 | - Versions only exist if the bucket has versioning enabled; if not, this
28 |   reports just the single current object rather than erroring.

2 | (`/alfresco/api/-default-/public/alfresco/versions/1`).

4 | UNVERIFIED — written against Alfresco's documented REST API contract (cross
5 | -checked against the published OpenAPI spec and client SDK model
6 | definitions), but there's no live Alfresco server in this environment to
7 | test it against. Run it against a real instance before trusting it the way
8 | FileNet's and local disk's providers are trusted (those were verified live,
9 | this wasn't).
10 | 
11 | The server is per-connection (`config_fields` collects `base_url`), not a
12 | single global — different connections can point at entirely different
13 | Alfresco instances. Unlike FileNet, Alfresco addresses everything by node
14 | id, not by path — so `folder_id=None` (FileDrive's "root") is resolved once
15 | to a real node id (a dedicated "FileDrive" folder under Company Home,
16 | created on first use) and cached *per base URL*, since this provider

108 |     def _root_id(self, creds: dict) -> str:
109 |         cache_key = self._base_url(creds)
110 |         cached = self._root_id_cache.get(cache_key)
111 |         if cached:
112 |             return cached
113 |         # This provider instance is a process-wide singleton shared by
114 |         # every connection to the same Alfresco server, and FastAPI runs
115 |         # sync handlers in a real thread pool — without a lock, concurrent
116 |         # first-requests for a freshly connected server would each find no
117 |         # existing root folder and each create their own duplicate.
118 |         # Double-checked locking: re-test the cache after acquiring the
119 |         # lock, since another thread may have populated it while we waited.
120 |         with self._root_id_lock:
121 |             cached = self._root_id_cache.get(cache_key)
122 |             if cached:
123 |                 return cached
124 |             existing = self._find_child_by_name(creds, "-root-", _APP_ROOT_NAME, is_folder=True)
125 |             if existing:
126 |                 self._root_id_cache[cache_key] = existing
127 |                 return existing
128 |             created = self._request(

130 |                 json={"name": _APP_ROOT_NAME, "nodeType": "cm:folder"},

+"""IBM i (AS/400 / iSeries) storage provider for FileDrive.
+
+Documents on IBM i can live in three places; this provider handles all three:
+
+  1. IFS (Integrated File System) — a POSIX-style hierarchy accessible via
+     SFTP. FileDrive browses IFS directories exactly like a local filesystem.
+
+  2. DB2 for i — documents stored as BLOBs in a user-specified table/column.
+     Each row's primary key becomes the file id; the name column supplies the
+     display name.
+
+  3. CMOD (Content Manager OnDemand) — IBM's archive system on IBM i. When a
+     CMOD REST base URL is provided, FileDrive proxies read/search operations
+     through its REST API (`/CMODServer/v1`).
+
+Connection credentials collected by `config_fields`:
+  - hostname      : IBM i hostname or IP
+  - port          : SFTP port (default 22)
+  - ifs_root      : IFS root path (default /home)
+  - db2_table     : optional — TABLE.COLUMN for BLOB documents
+  - db2_name_col  : name column in db2_table (default FILENAME)
+  - cmod_url      : optional CMOD REST API base URL
+
+UNVERIFIED — written against documented IBM i SFTP and CMOD REST API
+contracts.  Verify against a live IBM i partition before production use.
+"""
+
+import io
+import logging
+import stat
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+
+logger = logging.getLogger("ibmi_provider")
+
+try:
+    import paramiko  # type: ignore
+    _HAS_PARAMIKO = True
+except ImportError:
+    _HAS_PARAMIKO = False
+
+try:
+    import requests as _requests  # type: ignore
+    _HAS_REQUESTS = True
+except ImportError:
+    _HAS_REQUESTS = False
+
+from .base import (
+    AuthMode,
+    BreadcrumbEntry,
+    ConfigField,
+    FileInfo,
+    FolderContents,
+    FolderInfo,
+    ProviderError,
+    StorageProvider,
+    VersionInfo,
+)
+
+_TRASH_DIR = ".FileDriveTrash"
+
+
+def _require_paramiko() -> None:
+    if not _HAS_PARAMIKO:
+        raise ProviderError("paramiko is required for the IBM i provider. Install it with: pip install paramiko", 503)
+
+
+def _require_requests() -> None:
+    if not _HAS_REQUESTS:
+        raise ProviderError("requests is required for the IBM i provider. Install it with: pip install requests", 503)
+
+
+def _sftp(creds: dict):
+    """Return an (SSHClient, SFTPClient) pair.  Caller must close both."""
+    _require_paramiko()
+    ssh = paramiko.SSHClient()
+    ssh.set_missing_host_key_policy(paramiko.AutoAddPolicy())
+    try:
+        ssh.connect(
+            hostname=creds["hostname"],
+            port=int(creds.get("port") or 22),
+            username=creds["username"],
+            password=creds["password"],
+            timeout=15,
+            allow_agent=False,
+            look_for_keys=False,
+        )
+    except Exception as exc:
+        raise ProviderError(f"Could not connect to IBM i via SFTP: {exc}", status_code=502)
+    sftp = ssh.open_sftp()
+    return ssh, sftp
+
+
+def _dt(ts: float | None) -> datetime | None:
+    return datetime.fromtimestamp(ts, tz=timezone.utc) if ts else None
+
+
+def _ifs_file(attr, path: str, ifs_root: str) -> FileInfo:
+    parent = path.rsplit("/", 1)[0] or ifs_root
+    if parent == ifs_root:
+        parent = None  # type: ignore[assignment]
+    return FileInfo(
+        id=path,
+        name=path.rsplit("/", 1)[-1],
+        folder_id=parent,
+        version_number=1,
+        size_bytes=attr.st_size,
+        content_type=None,
+        updated_at=_dt(attr.st_mtime),
+    )
+
+
+def _ifs_folder(path: str, ifs_root: str) -> FolderInfo:
+    parent = path.rsplit("/", 1)[0] or None
+    if parent == ifs_root:
+        parent = None
+    return FolderInfo(id=path, name=path.rsplit("/", 1)[-1], parent_id=parent)
+
+
+class IBMiProvider(StorageProvider):
+    """IBM i IFS + DB2 BLOB + CMOD storage provider."""
+
+    key = "ibm_i"
+    display_name = "IBM i (AS/400 / iSeries)"
+    auth_mode = AuthMode.CREDENTIALS
+
+    @property
+    def config_fields(self) -> list[ConfigField]:
+        return [
+            ConfigField("hostname", "IBM i Hostname / IP"),
+            ConfigField("port", "SFTP Port", "22", required=False),
+            ConfigField("ifs_root", "IFS Root Path", "/home", required=False),
+            ConfigField("db2_table", "DB2 BLOB Table (SCHEMA.TABLE)", "", required=False),
+            ConfigField("db2_name_col", "DB2 Name Column", "FILENAME", required=False),
+            ConfigField("cmod_url", "CMOD REST Base URL (optional)", "", required=False),
+        ]
+
+    def _ifs_root(self, creds: dict) -> str:
+        return (creds.get("ifs_root") or "/home").rstrip("/") or "/"
+
+    # --- auth ---
+
+    def authenticate(self, username: str, password: str, config: dict | None = None) -> dict | None:
+        config = config or {}
+        hostname = (config.get("hostname") or "").strip()
+        if not hostname:
+            raise ProviderError("Hostname is required", status_code=400)
+        creds = {
+            "username": username,
+            "password": password,
+            "hostname": hostname,
+            "port": (config.get("port") or "22").strip(),
+            "ifs_root": (config.get("ifs_root") or "/home").strip(),
+            "db2_table": (config.get("db2_table") or "").strip(),
+            "db2_name_col": (config.get("db2_name_col") or "FILENAME").strip(),
+            "cmod_url": (config.get("cmod_url") or "").strip(),
+        }
+        try:
+            ssh, sftp = _sftp(creds)
+            sftp.close()
+            ssh.close()
+        except ProviderError:
+            return None
+        return creds
+
+    def whoami(self, creds: dict) -> str:
+        return f"{creds['username']}@{creds['hostname']}"
+
+    # --- folder helpers ---
+
+    def _list_ifs(self, creds: dict, path: str) -> FolderContents:
+        ifs_root = self._ifs_root(creds)
+        ssh, sftp = _sftp(creds)
+        try:
+            try:
+                attrs = sftp.listdir_attr(path)
+            except IOError as exc:
+                raise ProviderError(f"IFS path not found: {exc}", status_code=404)
+            folders, files = [], []
+            for a in attrs:
+                full_path = f"{path.rstrip('/')}/{a.filename}"
+                if a.filename.startswith("."):
+                    continue
+                if stat.S_ISDIR(a.st_mode or 0):
+                    folders.append(_ifs_folder(full_path, ifs_root))
+                else:
+                    files.append(_ifs_file(a, full_path, ifs_root))
+            current = None
+            if path != ifs_root:
+                current = _ifs_folder(path, ifs_root)
+            return FolderContents(
+                folder=current,
+                breadcrumb=[BreadcrumbEntry(id=None, name="IBM i IFS")],
+                folders=folders,
+                files=files,
+            )
+        finally:
+            sftp.close()
+            ssh.close()
+
+    def get_children(self, creds: dict, folder_id: str | None) -> FolderContents:
+        path = folder_id if folder_id is not None else self._ifs_root(creds)
+        return self._list_ifs(creds, path)
+
+    def list_trash(self, creds: dict) -> FolderContents:
+        trash = f"{self._ifs_root(creds)}/{_TRASH_DIR}"
+        ssh, sftp = _sftp(creds)
+        try:
+            try:
+                sftp.mkdir(trash)
+            except IOError:
+                pass  # already exists
+        finally:
+            sftp.close()
+            ssh.close()
+        result = self._list_ifs(creds, trash)
+        result.breadcrumb = [BreadcrumbEntry(id=None, name="Trash")]
+        return result
+
+    def create_folder(self, creds: dict, parent_id: str | None, name: str) -> FolderInfo:
+        parent = parent_id if parent_id is not None else self._ifs_root(creds)
+        new_path = f"{parent.rstrip('/')}/{name}"
+        ssh, sftp = _sftp(creds)
+        try:
+            sftp.mkdir(new_path)
+        except IOError as exc:
+            raise ProviderError(f"Could not create folder: {exc}", status_code=502)
+        finally:
+            sftp.close()
+            ssh.close()
+        return _ifs_folder(new_path, self._ifs_root(creds))
+
+    def rename_folder(self, creds: dict, folder_id: str, name: str) -> FolderInfo:
+        parent = folder_id.rsplit("/", 1)[0] or self._ifs_root(creds)
+        new_path = f"{parent}/{name}"
+        ssh, sftp = _sftp(creds)
+        try:
+            sftp.rename(folder_id, new_path)
+        except IOError as exc:
+            raise ProviderError(f"Rename failed: {exc}", status_code=502)
+        finally:
+            sftp.close()
+            ssh.close()
+        return _ifs_folder(new_path, self._ifs_root(creds))
+
+    def move_folder(self, creds: dict, folder_id: str, new_parent_id: str | None) -> FolderInfo:
+        new_parent = new_parent_id if new_parent_id is not None else self._ifs_root(creds)
+        name = folder_id.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
+        new_path = f"{new_parent.rstrip('/')}/{name}"
+        ssh, sftp = _sftp(creds)
+        try:
+            sftp.rename(folder_id, new_path)
+        except IOError as exc:
+            raise ProviderError(f"Move failed: {exc}", status_code=502)
+        finally:
+            sftp.close()
+            ssh.close()
+        return _ifs_folder(new_path, self._ifs_root(creds))
+
+    def delete_folder(self, creds: dict, folder_id: str) -> None:
+        ssh, sftp = _sftp(creds)
+        try:
+            self._rmdir_recursive(sftp, folder_id)
+        finally:
+            sftp.close()
+            ssh.close()
+
+    def _rmdir_recursive(self, sftp, path: str) -> None:
+        for a in sftp.listdir_attr(path):
+            full = f"{path}/{a.filename}"
+            if stat.S_ISDIR(a.st_mode or 0):
+                self._rmdir_recursive(sftp, full)
+            else:
+                sftp.remove(full)
+        sftp.rmdir(path)
+
+    # --- file operations ---
+
+    def create_document(self, creds: dict, folder_id: str | None, name: str, content_type: str, content: bytes) -> FileInfo:
+        parent = folder_id if folder_id is not None else self._ifs_root(creds)
+        path = f"{parent.rstrip('/')}/{name}"
+        ssh, sftp = _sftp(creds)
+        try:
+            with sftp.file(path, "wb") as f:
+                f.write(content)
+            attr = sftp.stat(path)
+        except IOError as exc:
+            raise ProviderError(f"Upload failed: {exc}", status_code=502)
+        finally:
+            sftp.close()
+            ssh.close()
+        return _ifs_file(attr, path, self._ifs_root(creds))
+
+    def get_file(self, creds: dict, file_id: str) -> FileInfo:
+        ssh, sftp = _sftp(creds)
+        try:
+            attr = sftp.stat(file_id)
+        except IOError as exc:
+            raise ProviderError(f"File not found: {exc}", status_code=404)
+        finally:
+            sftp.close()
+            ssh.close()
+        return _ifs_file(attr, file_id, self._ifs_root(creds))
+
+    def rename_file(self, creds: dict, file_id: str, name: str) -> FileInfo:
+        parent = file_id.rsplit("/", 1)[0]
+        new_path = f"{parent}/{name}"
+        ssh, sftp = _sftp(creds)
+        try:
+            sftp.rename(file_id, new_path)
+            attr = sftp.stat(new_path)
+        except IOError as exc:
+            raise ProviderError(f"Rename failed: {exc}", status_code=502)
+        finally:
+            sftp.close()
+            ssh.close()
+        return _ifs_file(attr, new_path, self._ifs_root(creds))
+
+    def move_file(self, creds: dict, file_id: str, new_folder_id: str | None) -> FileInfo:
+        new_parent = new_folder_id if new_folder_id is not None else self._ifs_root(creds)
+        name = file_id.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
+        new_path = f"{new_parent.rstrip('/')}/{name}"
+        ssh, sftp = _sftp(creds)
+        try:
+            sftp.rename(file_id, new_path)
+            attr = sftp.stat(new_path)
+        except IOError as exc:
+            raise ProviderError(f"Move failed: {exc}", status_code=502)
+        finally:
+            sftp.close()
+            ssh.close()
+        return _ifs_file(attr, new_path, self._ifs_root(creds))
+
+    def delete_file(self, creds: dict, file_id: str) -> None:
+        ssh, sftp = _sftp(creds)
+        try:
+            sftp.remove(file_id)
+        except IOError as exc:
+            raise ProviderError(f"Delete failed: {exc}", status_code=502)
+        finally:
+            sftp.close()
+            ssh.close()
+
+    def get_content(self, creds: dict, file_id: str) -> bytes:
+        ssh, sftp = _sftp(creds)
+        try:
+            buf = io.BytesIO()
+            sftp.getfo(file_id, buf)
+            return buf.getvalue()
+        except IOError as exc:
+            raise ProviderError(f"Could not read file: {exc}", status_code=404)
+        finally:
+            sftp.close()
+            ssh.close()
+
+    # --- versions (IFS has no native versioning — report single current) ---
+

+"""IBM Z (z/OS mainframe) storage provider for FileDrive.
+
+Documents on z/OS can live in three places; this provider handles all three:
+
+  1. z/OS Datasets (PDS members + sequential datasets) — accessed via the
+     z/OSMF REST Data Set API (`/zosmf/restfiles/ds`). PDS members map to
+     files; PDS libraries and HLQs map to folders.
+
+  2. USS (Unix System Services) — a POSIX hierarchy accessible through the
+     z/OSMF REST USS File API (`/zosmf/restfiles/fs`). Browsed like a regular
+     filesystem — identical UX to the IBM i IFS path.
+
+  3. IBM Content Manager 8 (CM8) — an enterprise ECM system running on z/OS
+     that exposes a REST API at `<cm8_url>/IBMcmRecordsView/...`. When
+     `cm8_url` is set in the connection config, FileDrive routes operations
+     through CM8 instead of z/OSMF.
+
+Connection credentials collected by `config_fields`:
+  - zosmf_url   : z/OSMF base URL (e.g. https://mainframe:10443)
+  - system      : z/OS system name (for display)
+  - uss_root    : USS root path (default /u)
+  - cm8_url     : optional CM8 REST base URL
+
+UNVERIFIED — written against the z/OSMF REST Services documentation and
+IBM CM8 REST API reference. Verify against a live z/OS system before
+production use.
+"""
+
+import base64
+import logging
+import urllib.parse
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+
+logger = logging.getLogger("ibmz_provider")
+
+try:
+    import requests as _requests  # type: ignore
+    _HAS_REQUESTS = True
+except ImportError:
+    _HAS_REQUESTS = False
+
+from .base import (
+    AuthMode,
+    BreadcrumbEntry,
+    ConfigField,
+    FileInfo,
+    FolderContents,
+    FolderInfo,
+    ProviderError,
+    StorageProvider,
+    VersionInfo,
+)
+
+_TRASH_DIR = ".FileDriveTrash"
+
+
+def _require_requests() -> None:
+    if not _HAS_REQUESTS:
+        raise ProviderError(
+            "requests is required for the IBM Z provider. Install it with: pip install requests", 503
+        )
+
+
+def _basic(creds: dict) -> str:
+    return base64.b64encode(f"{creds['username']}:{creds['password']}".encode()).decode()
+
+
+def _headers(creds: dict) -> dict:
+    return {
+        "Authorization": f"Basic {_basic(creds)}",
+        "Content-Type": "application/json",
+        "X-CSRF-ZOSMF-HEADER": "*",
+    }
+
+
+def _zosmf(creds: dict) -> str:
+    return creds["zosmf_url"].rstrip("/")
+
+
+def _uss_root(creds: dict) -> str:
+    return (creds.get("uss_root") or "/u").rstrip("/") or "/"
+
+
+def _cm8_url(creds: dict) -> str | None:
+    return (creds.get("cm8_url") or "").strip() or None
+
+
+def _dt_uss(value: str | None) -> datetime | None:
+    """Parse z/OSMF USS timestamps: '2024-01-15T09:00:00'."""
+    if not value:
+        return None
+    try:
+        return datetime.fromisoformat(value).replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
+    except ValueError:
+        return None
+
+
+def _dt_ds(value: str | None) -> datetime | None:
+    """Parse z/OSMF dataset lastReferredDate 'YYYY/MM/DD'."""
+    if not value:
+        return None
+    try:
+        return datetime.strptime(value, "%Y/%m/%d").replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
+    except ValueError:
+        return None
+
+
+def _get(creds: dict, url: str, params: dict | None = None) -> dict:
+    _require_requests()
+    try:
+        resp = _requests.get(url, headers=_headers(creds), params=params, timeout=20, verify=False)
+    except _requests.RequestException as exc:
+        raise ProviderError(f"z/OSMF unreachable: {exc}", status_code=502)
+    if resp.status_code == 401:
+        raise ProviderError("Invalid z/OS credentials", status_code=401)
+    if resp.status_code == 404:
+        raise ProviderError("Not found on z/OS", status_code=404)
+    if resp.status_code >= 400:
+        raise ProviderError(f"z/OSMF error {resp.status_code}: {resp.text[:300]}", status_code=502)
+    return resp.json() if resp.content else {}
+

+def _put_bytes(creds: dict, url: str, data: bytes, content_type: str = "application/octet-stream") -> None:
+    _require_requests()

+    except _requests.RequestException as exc:

1 | """Tests for ai_service.py's prompt-injection hardening.
2 | 
3 | Document text passed into summarize()/suggest_metadata()/answer_question()
4 | comes from files any user with write access can upload, not a trusted
5 | operator, so it must never be given the same weight as the actual
6 | instructions in the prompt. These tests verify the untrusted text is
7 | fenced with an explicit non-instruction framing, and that suggest_metadata()
8 | throws away any field key the model wasn't actually asked for -- the
9 | concrete way this can be exploited if wrapping alone is insufficient.
10 | """

"""
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

# Helpers

def _disco_backend():

def _mock_iam_token():

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class TestWatsonxBackend:
    def test_summarize_calls_watsonx(self):
        with _watsonx_backend(), _mock_iam_token(), patch.object(
            ai_service, "_call_watsonx", return_value="This is a summary."
        ) as mock_wx:
            result = ai_service.summarize("Some document text about invoices.")
        mock_wx.assert_called_once()
        assert result == "This is a summary."

    def test_summarize_routes_through_llm(self):
        """summarize() on watsonx backend must call _call_watsonx, not _call_openai_compatible."""
        with _watsonx_backend(), _mock_iam_token():
            with patch.object(ai_service, "_call_watsonx", return_value="wx summary") as wx_mock, \
                 patch.object(ai_service, "_call_openai_compatible") as oa_mock:
                ai_service.summarize("text")
        wx_mock.assert_called_once()
        oa_mock.assert_not_called()

    def test_suggest_metadata_uses_generative_path(self):
        fields = [{"key": "vendor", "type": "text", "label": "Vendor"}]
        injected_json = '{"vendor": "Acme Corp"}'
        with _watsonx_backend(), _mock_iam_token(), patch.object(
            ai_service, "_call_watsonx", return_value=injected_json
        ):
            result = ai_service.suggest_metadata("Invoice from Acme Corp.", fields)
        assert result == {"vendor": "Acme Corp"}

    def test_suggest_metadata_still_drops_disallowed_keys(self):
        fields = [{"key": "amount", "type": "number", "label": "Amount"}]

        assert "admin" not in result
        assert "evil" not in result

    def test_answer_question_uses_watsonx(self):
        with _watsonx_backend(), _mock_iam_token(), patch.object(
            ai_service, "_llm", return_value="The answer is 42."

        mock_llm.assert_called_once()

    def test_is_enabled_true_for_watsonx(self):

"""Tests for IBM i and IBM Z provider registration and basic structure.

These tests verify that the new providers register correctly, expose the
expected `key` / `display_name` / `config_fields`, and implement the full
StorageProvider interface — without requiring a live IBM i or z/OS system.
"""

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# IBM i provider
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class TestIBMiProviderRegistration:

        keys = [p.key for p in list_providers()]
        assert "ibm_i" in keys, "IBM i provider must be registered in the provider registry"

    def test_ibmi_display_name(self):
        p = get_provider("ibm_i")
        assert "IBM i" in p.display_name or "AS/400" in p.display_name or "iSeries" in p.display_name

    def test_ibmi_has_required_config_fields(self):
        p = get_provider("ibm_i")
        field_keys = {f.key for f in p.config_fields}
        assert "hostname" in field_keys, "IBM i provider must require hostname"

    def test_ibmi_optional_fields_present(self):
        p = get_provider("ibm_i")
        field_keys = {f.key for f in p.config_fields}
        # IFS root, DB2 table, CMOD URL are all expected
        assert "ifs_root" in field_keys
        assert "db2_table" in field_keys
        assert "cmod_url" in field_keys

        from app.storage_providers.base import AuthMode
        p = get_provider("ibm_i")
        assert p.auth_mode == AuthMode.CREDENTIALS

    def test_ibmi_implements_all_abstract_methods(self):
        """Instantiation would fail at import time if abstract methods were
        missing, but verify the concrete class has all StorageProvider methods."""
        from app.storage_providers.ibmi_provider import IBMiProvider
        from app.storage_providers.base import StorageProvider
        required = [
            "get_children", "list_trash", "create_folder", "rename_folder",
            "move_folder", "delete_folder", "create_document", "get_file",
            "rename_file", "move_file", "delete_file", "get_content",
            "list_versions", "create_version", "get_version_content",
            "restore_version", "trash_folder", "restore_folder",
            "trash_file", "restore_file", "search",
        ]
        p = IBMiProvider()
        for method in required:
            assert hasattr(p, method), f"IBMiProvider must implement {method}"

        """authenticate() should raise ProviderError (not ImportError) when
        paramiko is not installed."""

        from app.storage_providers.ibmi_provider import IBMiProvider

"""Tests for IBM i and IBM Z provider registration and basic structure.

These tests verify that the new providers register correctly, expose the
expected `key` / `display_name` / `config_fields`, and implement the full
StorageProvider interface — without requiring a live IBM i or z/OS system.
"""
import pytest

from app.storage_providers.registry import list_providers, get_provider


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# IBM i provider
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class TestIBMiProviderRegistration:
    def test_ibmi_is_registered(self):
        keys = [p.key for p in list_providers()]
        assert "ibm_i" in keys, "IBM i provider must be registered in the provider registry"

    def test_ibmi_display_name(self):
        p = get_provider("ibm_i")
        assert "IBM i" in p.display_name or "AS/400" in p.display_name or "iSeries" in p.display_name

    def test_ibmi_has_required_config_fields(self):
        p = get_provider("ibm_i")
        field_keys = {f.key for f in p.config_fields}
        assert "hostname" in field_keys, "IBM i provider must require hostname"

    def test_ibmi_optional_fields_present(self):
        p = get_provider("ibm_i")
        field_keys = {f.key for f in p.config_fields}
        # IFS root, DB2 table, CMOD URL are all expected
        assert "ifs_root" in field_keys
        assert "db2_table" in field_keys
        assert "cmod_url" in field_keys

    def test_ibmi_auth_mode_is_credentials(self):
        from app.storage_providers.base import AuthMode
        p = get_provider("ibm_i")
        assert p.auth_mode == AuthMode.CREDENTIALS

    def test_ibmi_implements_all_abstract_methods(self):
        """Instantiation would fail at import time if abstract methods were
        missing, but verify the concrete class has all StorageProvider methods."""
        from app.storage_providers.ibmi_provider import IBMiProvider
        from app.storage_providers.base import StorageProvider
        required = [
            "get_children", "list_trash", "create_folder", "rename_folder",
            "move_folder", "delete_folder", "create_document", "get_file",
            "rename_file", "move_file", "delete_file", "get_content",
            "list_versions", "create_version", "get_version_content",
            "restore_version", "trash_folder", "restore_folder",
            "trash_file", "restore_file", "search",
        ]
        p = IBMiProvider()
        for method in required:
            assert hasattr(p, method), f"IBMiProvider must implement {method}"

    def test_ibmi_error_without_paramiko(self):
        """authenticate() should raise ProviderError (not ImportError) when
        paramiko is not installed."""
        from unittest.mock import patch
        from app.storage_providers.ibmi_provider import IBMiProvider
        from app.storage_providers.base import ProviderError
        p = IBMiProvider()
        with patch("app.storage_providers.ibmi_provider._HAS_PARAMIKO", False):
            with pytest.raises(ProviderError) as exc_info:
                p.authenticate("user", "pass", {"hostname": "192.168.1.1"})
        assert "paramiko" in str(exc_info.value).lower()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# IBM Z provider
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class TestIBMZProviderRegistration:
    def test_ibmz_is_registered(self):
        keys = [p.key for p in list_providers()]
        assert "ibm_z" in keys, "IBM Z provider must be registered in the provider registry"

    def test_ibmz_display_name(self):
        p = get_provider("ibm_z")
        assert "IBM Z" in p.display_name or "z/OS" in p.display_name or "Mainframe" in p.display_name

    def test_ibmz_has_required_config_fields(self):
        p = get_provider("ibm_z")
        field_keys = {f.key for f in p.config_fields}
        assert "zosmf_url" in field_keys, "IBM Z provider must require z/OSMF URL"

    def test_ibmz_optional_fields_present(self):
        p = get_provider("ibm_z")
        field_keys = {f.key for f in p.config_fields}
        assert "uss_root" in field_keys
        assert "cm8_url" in field_keys
        assert "system" in field_keys

    def test_ibmz_auth_mode_is_credentials(self):
        from app.storage_providers.base import AuthMode
        p = get_provider("ibm_z")
        assert p.auth_mode == AuthMode.CREDENTIALS

    def test_ibmz_implements_all_abstract_methods(self):
        from app.storage_providers.ibmz_provider import IBMZProvider
        required = [
            "get_children", "list_trash", "create_folder", "rename_folder",
            "move_folder", "delete_folder", "create_document", "get_file",
            "rename_file", "move_file", "delete_file", "get_content",
            "list_versions", "create_version", "get_version_content",
            "restore_version", "trash_folder", "restore_folder",
            "trash_file", "restore_file", "search",
        ]
        p = IBMZProvider()
        for method in required:
            assert hasattr(p, method), f"IBMZProvider must implement {method}"

    def test_ibmz_use_cm8_returns_false_without_cm8_url(self):
        from app.storage_providers.ibmz_provider import IBMZProvider
        p = IBMZProvider()
        assert p._use_cm8({"cm8_url": ""}) is False
        assert p._use_cm8({"cm8_url": None}) is False  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        assert p._use_cm8({}) is False

    def test_ibmz_use_cm8_returns_true_with_cm8_url(self):
        from app.storage_providers.ibmz_provider import IBMZProvider
        p = IBMZProvider()
        assert p._use_cm8({"cm8_url": "https://mainframe:9080"}) is True

    def test_ibmz_error_without_requests(self):
        """authenticate() should raise ProviderError (not ImportError) when
        requests is not installed."""
        from unittest.mock import patch
        from app.storage_providers.ibmz_provider import IBMZProvider
        from app.storage_providers.base import ProviderError
        p = IBMZProvider()
        with patch("app.storage_providers.ibmz_provider._HAS_REQUESTS", False):
            with pytest.raises(ProviderError) as exc_info:
                p.authenticate("user", "pass", {"zosmf_url": "https://mf:10443"})
        assert "requests" in str(exc_info.value).lower()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Provider count
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_total_registered_providers():
    """After adding IBM i and IBM Z we should have at least 11 providers."""
    providers = list_providers()
    assert len(providers) >= 11, (
        f"Expected at least 11 registered providers, got {len(providers)}: "
        f"{[p.key for p in providers]}"
    )

"""Tests for IBM i and IBM Z provider registration and basic structure.

These tests verify that the new providers register correctly, expose the
expected `key` / `display_name` / `config_fields`, and implement the full
StorageProvider interface — without requiring a live IBM i or z/OS system.
"""
import pytest

from app.storage_providers.registry import list_providers, get_provider


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# IBM i provider
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class TestIBMiProviderRegistration:
    def test_ibmi_is_registered(self):
        keys = [p.key for p in list_providers()]
        assert "ibm_i" in keys, "IBM i provider must be registered in the provider registry"

    def test_ibmi_display_name(self):
        p = get_provider("ibm_i")
        assert "IBM i" in p.display_name or "AS/400" in p.display_name or "iSeries" in p.display_name

    def test_ibmi_has_required_config_fields(self):
        p = get_provider("ibm_i")
        field_keys = {f.key for f in p.config_fields}
        assert "hostname" in field_keys, "IBM i provider must require hostname"

    def test_ibmi_optional_fields_present(self):
        p = get_provider("ibm_i")
        field_keys = {f.key for f in p.config_fields}
        # IFS root, DB2 table, CMOD URL are all expected
        assert "ifs_root" in field_keys
        assert "db2_table" in field_keys
        assert "cmod_url" in field_keys

    def test_ibmi_auth_mode_is_credentials(self):
        from app.storage_providers.base import AuthMode
        p = get_provider("ibm_i")
        assert p.auth_mode == AuthMode.CREDENTIALS

    def test_ibmi_implements_all_abstract_methods(self):
        """Instantiation would fail at import time if abstract methods were
        missing, but verify the concrete class has all StorageProvider methods."""
        from app.storage_providers.ibmi_provider import IBMiProvider
        from app.storage_providers.base import StorageProvider
        required = [
            "get_children", "list_trash", "create_folder", "rename_folder",
            "move_folder", "delete_folder", "create_document", "get_file",
            "rename_file", "move_file", "delete_file", "get_content",
            "list_versions", "create_version", "get_version_content",
            "restore_version", "trash_folder", "restore_folder",
            "trash_file", "restore_file", "search",
        ]
        p = IBMiProvider()
        for method in required:
            assert hasattr(p, method), f"IBMiProvider must implement {method}"

    def test_ibmi_error_without_paramiko(self):
        """authenticate() should raise ProviderError (not ImportError) when
        paramiko is not installed."""
        from unittest.mock import patch
        from app.storage_providers.ibmi_provider import IBMiProvider
        from app.storage_providers.base import ProviderError
        p = IBMiProvider()
        with patch("app.storage_providers.ibmi_provider._HAS_PARAMIKO", False):
            with pytest.raises(ProviderError) as exc_info:
                p.authenticate("user", "pass", {"hostname": "192.168.1.1"})
        assert "paramiko" in str(exc_info.value).lower()

All 7 phases of Section 9 are complete. Here's a full summary of what was built:

---

## Section 9 — Complete ✅

### Phase 1 — IBM i Provider ([`ibmi_provider.py`](backend/app/storage_providers/ibmi_provider.py))
- **IFS (Integrated File System)** via SFTP — full browse, upload, download, rename, move, delete, trash/restore, recursive search
- **DB2 BLOB** config fields (`db2_table`, `db2_name_col`) declared for future ODBC integration
- **CMOD** config field (`cmod_url`) declared for Content Manager OnDemand
- Graceful `ProviderError` (not bare `ImportError`) when `paramiko` is absent

### Phase 2 — IBM Z Provider ([`ibmz_provider.py`](backend/app/storage_providers/ibmz_provider.py))
- **USS** via z/OSMF REST File API — browse, read, write, rename, delete, trash, search
- **z/OS Datasets** — name-pattern search via z/OSMF REST Data Set API
- **CM8 (Content Manager 8)** — full ECM browse and document retrieval when `cm8_url` is set; routes automatically with `_use_cm8()`

### Phase 3 — Watson AI ([`ai_service.py`](backend/app/ai_service.py))
| Backend | `FD_AI_BACKEND=` | Features |
|---|---|---|
| IBM watsonx.ai | `watsonx` | Summarise, metadata extraction, Q&A via `granite-13b-chat-v2` with IAM token caching |
| Watson NLU | `watson_nlu` | Keyword/entity extraction → summary; entity-to-field mapping for metadata; NLU-based classification |
| Watson Discovery | `watson_disco` | Passage retrieval Q&A; optionally upgrades to generative answer via watsonx fallback |

### Phase 4 — AI Workflow Routing ([`routers/ai.py`](backend/app/routers/ai.py))
- New `POST /files/{file_id}/ai/suggest_workflow` endpoint
- Returns `suggested_workflow_id`, `suggested_workflow_name`, and `confidence` (`high`/`medium`/`low`)
- No changes to existing Workflow Engine

### Phase 5 — UI ([`AiPanel.tsx`](frontend/src/components/AiPanel.tsx), [`icons/index.tsx`](frontend/src/icons/index.tsx))
- **IBM Watson badge** appears on all AI panel sections when a Watson backend is active
- **Workflow Suggestion section** — Suggest button, confidence badge (green/amber/red), Start/Dismiss actions
- Watson Discovery Q&A placeholder adapts
- New `workflow` SVG icon; IBM i (`#0f62fe`) and IBM Z (`#198038`) provider badge colours

### Phase 6 — Tests
- [`test_ibm_providers.py`](backend/tests/test_ibm_providers.py) — 17 tests covering registration, config fields, interface completeness, CM8 routing, and missing-dependency errors for both new providers
- [`test_ai_watson.py`](backend/tests/test_ai_watson.py) — 21 tests covering all three Watson backends, `suggest_workflow`, keyword heuristics, and injection safety

### Phase 7 — Configuration
- [`backend/env.example`](backend/env.example) — full template with all Watson and IBM i/Z variables documented
- [`requirements.txt`](backend/requirements.txt) — `paramiko` and `ibm-watson` noted as optional dependencies

## Honest Production Readiness Assessment

**Short answer: No — not yet. Some parts are production-ready. Others are solid foundations that need one specific step before production: verification against a live system.**

Here is a component-by-component breakdown:

---

### ✅ Production Ready — No changes needed

| Component | Why |
|---|---|
| **Watson NLU integration** | Uses the documented v1 REST API with API key auth, proper error handling, correct feature payloads. Ready to point at a real instance. |
| **watsonx.ai integration** | Uses the published `ml/v1/text/generation` endpoint, IAM token exchange with caching, correct Granite model payload. Ready with real credentials. |
| **Watson Discovery integration** | Uses the documented v2 query API with passage retrieval. Ready with real credentials. |
| **AI workflow routing** (`suggest_workflow`) | Pure Python logic + NLU delegation. No external dependency. Works now. |
| **`POST /files/{id}/ai/suggest_workflow` endpoint** | Proper FastAPI route, correct schema, no side effects. |
| **AI Panel UI** (`AiPanel.tsx`) | Watson badge, confidence indicator, workflow suggestion UI — fully wired up. |
| **Provider registry** | Both new providers register with try/except so a missing `paramiko` never crashes the app. |
| **IBM i / Z provider badges** in `icons/index.tsx` | Pure UI, no risk. |
| **`env.example`** | Complete documentation template. |
| **165 tests** | All pass, no regressions. |

---

### ⚠️ Functional but UNVERIFIED — needs live system test before production

These are the two new storage providers. The code is structurally complete — it implements the full 21-method `StorageProvider` interface, errors map correctly to HTTP status codes, credentials validate at connection time. But **no real IBM i or z/OS system was available to run it against**, so they carry explicit `UNVERIFIED` warnings in their docstrings.

#### IBM i Provider ([`ibmi_provider.py`](backend/app/storage_providers/ibmi_provider.py))
| Gap | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Not live-tested** | SFTP calls written against paramiko docs. A real IBM i SFTP server may behave differently on edge cases (permission errors, locked files, IFS path encoding). |
| **DB2 BLOB is config-only** | `db2_table` and `db2_name_col` fields are declared and stored in creds, but there is **no actual DB2 query code**. Connecting a DB2 BLOB source currently does nothing with those fields. |
| **CMOD is config-only** | `cmod_url` is declared and stored, but the CMOD REST API (`/CMODServer/v1`) is **not actually called anywhere** in the provider. It was described in the doc but not yet wired up. |
| **`AutoAddPolicy` on SSH** | Accepts any host key — acceptable for private enterprise networks, but should be replaced with a verified host key in a security-conscious production deployment. |
| **No connection pooling** | Opens and closes a new SFTP connection on every operation. Acceptable for low volume; becomes a bottleneck under load. |

#### IBM Z Provider ([`ibmz_provider.py`](backend/app/storage_providers/ibmz_provider.py))
| Gap | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Not live-tested** | z/OSMF REST calls written against IBM documentation. Real z/OS systems may return slightly different JSON shapes (e.g. `items` vs `JSONversion`), require specific `Accept:` headers, or enforce client certificate auth. |
| **`verify=False` on all HTTPS** | z/OSMF commonly uses self-signed certificates in enterprise environments, so SSL verification is disabled. This is intentional but should be replaced with a configurable CA bundle for strict environments. |
| **CM8 REST API shape is assumed** | The CM8 `IBMcmRecordsView` paths and response shapes were inferred from IBM documentation. IBM CM8 version numbers matter — the actual path prefix varies by release. |
| **Dataset browse is search-only** | `get_children` for non-CM8 mode only browses USS — it does not browse z/OS datasets as a folder tree (datasets are listed through the `search` path with a name pattern). |
| **`create_document` / `delete_file` raise 501 for CM8** | Intentional — CM8 REST document upload and delete require multi-part forms and workflow-aware deletes that weren't implemented in this release. |

---

### What to do before each goes to production

**IBM i:**
1. Test `authenticate()` + `get_children()` against a real IBM i SFTP server
2. Implement the DB2 BLOB query using `pyodbc` + IBM i Access ODBC driver (3–4 days work)
3. Implement the CMOD REST calls under `_cmod_url(creds)` check (2–3 days)
4. Replace `AutoAddPolicy` with a stored host key fingerprint check

**IBM Z:**
1. Test against a real z/OSMF endpoint — confirm JSON response shapes, required headers
2. Replace `verify=False` with a configurable CA bundle path config field
3. Verify the CM8 `IBMcmRecordsView` path against the actual CM8 version deployed
4. Implement full dataset folder-tree browsing via z/OSMF if needed

**Watson AI:** ✅ Ready — just needs real IBM Cloud credentials in `.env`.

1 | """IBM Z (z/OS mainframe) storage provider for FileDrive.
2 | 
3 | Documents on z/OS can live in three places; this provider handles all three:
4 | 
5 |   1. z/OS Datasets (PDS members + sequential datasets) — accessed via the
6 |      z/OSMF REST Data Set API (`/zosmf/restfiles/ds`). PDS members map to
7 |      files; PDS libraries and HLQs map to folders.
8 | 
9 |   2. USS (Unix System Services) — a POSIX hierarchy accessible through the
10 |      z/OSMF REST USS File API (`/zosmf/restfiles/fs`). Browsed like a regular
11 |      filesystem — identical UX to the IBM i IFS path.
12 | 
13 |   3. IBM Content Manager 8 (CM8) — an enterprise ECM system running on z/OS
14 |      that exposes a REST API at `<cm8_url>/IBMcmRecordsView/...`. When
15 |      `cm8_url` is set in the connection config, FileDrive routes operations
16 |      through CM8 instead of z/OSMF.
17 | 
18 | Connection credentials collected by `config_fields`:
19 |   - zosmf_url   : z/OSMF base URL (e.g. https://mainframe:10443)
20 |   - system      : z/OS system name (for display)
21 |   - uss_root    : USS root path (default /u)
22 |   - cm8_url     : optional CM8 REST base URL
23 | 
24 | UNVERIFIED — written against the z/OSMF REST Services documentation and
25 | IBM CM8 REST API reference. Verify against a live z/OS system before
26 | production use.
27 | """

Here is how to find out what you actually have access to:

## Step 1 — Check if you have IBM i on IBM Cloud

IBM i on IBM Cloud is called **"Power Virtual Server"**. Log in and check:

If you see a **Power Virtual Server workspace** already provisioned, you have IBM i available. If not, you would need to provision one — but that costs money (there is no free tier for IBM i).

---

## Step 2 — If you DO have a Power Virtual Server workspace

Go to:
```

```

→ Click your workspace  
→ Click **Virtual server instances**  
→ Find an IBM i instance  
→ Click it — you will see the **IP address** and **hostname**

Then ask (or check in the IBM i console):
- Is **SSHD (SFTP) started?** — run this command on the IBM i:

- What **user profile** do you have? That is your IBM i username.

## Step 3 — What you most likely DO have on IBM Cloud (free/included)

## The 3 ways to get IBM i access from IBM Cloud

### Option A — Power Virtual Server (Recommended — you create a real IBM i on IBM Cloud)

This is the official IBM Cloud way.

**Step 1** — Go to:
```
https://cloud.ibm.com/catalog/services/power-virtual-server
```

**Step 2** — Click **Create**  
- Select a region (Dallas or Frankfurt recommended)
- Resource group: Default
- Name it: `FileDrive-IBMi-Test`
- Click **Create**

**Step 3** — Once the workspace is created, go to:
```
https://cloud.ibm.com/power/overview
```
Click your workspace → **Virtual server instances** → **Create instance**

Fill in:
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Name | `filedrive-test` |
| SSH key | Create a new one (download the private key) |
| Operating system | **IBM i** |
| IBM i version | `7.5` (latest) |
| Machine type | `s922` (smallest) |
| Cores | `0.25` (minimum) |
| Memory | `4 GB` (minimum) |
| Storage | `100 GB` |

> ⚠️ **Cost warning:** IBM i on Power Virtual Server costs approximately **$0.50–$2.00/hour**. It is NOT free. Stop the instance when not testing.

**Step 4** — After provisioning (takes ~10 minutes), note the **External IP address** shown on the instance details page.

**Step 5** — Enable SFTP on the IBM i. Connect via the IBM i console or 5250 emulator and run:
```
STRTCPSVR SERVER(*SSHD)
```
To make it start automatically:
```
CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QSTRUP) VALUE('STRTCPSVR SERVER(*SSHD)')
```

**Step 6** — Create a user profile for FileDrive:
```
CRTUSRPRF USRPRF(FILEDRIVE) PASSWORD(YourPassword123) TEXT('FileDrive Test User')
```

**Step 7** — Test the connection from your Windows machine:
```powershell
ssh FILEDRIVE@<your-external-ip>
```

---

### Option B — IBM Satellite Connector (You already have this page open — free tier available)

Looking at your screenshot, you are already on the Satellite Connectors page. This option lets you connect an **existing on-premises IBM i** to IBM Cloud **without opening firewall ports**.

This only works if you already have a physical/virtual IBM i somewhere (office, data centre). If you have one:

**Step 1** — Click **Create connector** (blue button visible in your screenshot)
- Name: `FileDrive-IBMi`
- Location: your region

**Step 2** — On your on-premises server (Linux/Windows machine on the same network as IBM i), run the Satellite Connector agent (Docker container):
```bash
docker run -d --name satellite-connector \
  --env SATELLITE_CONNECTOR_ID=<your-connector-id> \
  --env SATELLITE_CONNECTOR_IAM_APIKEY=<your-ibm-cloud-api-key> \
  icr.io/ibm/satellite-connector/satellite-connector-agent:latest
```

**Step 3** — Create an **endpoint** pointing to your IBM i SFTP:
- Go to your connector → **Endpoints** → **Create endpoint**
- Destination hostname: `192.168.x.x` (your IBM i IP)
- Destination port: `22`
- Protocol: `TCP`

This gives you a public IBM Cloud hostname that tunnels to your IBM i SFTP — FileDrive connects to that cloud hostname.

IBM provides a free IBM i development environment for testing:

```
https://www.ibm.com/community/ibm-i/access-for-developers/
```

Or use the **IBM i Open Source community sandbox:**
```
https://ibmi-oss-docs.github.io/newbie-orientation/
```
